# Synthetic Tutoring Intervention: A Simulated Classroom Study

Alex Example. 2026. Locally authored synthetic source.

## Provenance
This document and its author are fictional. All participants, procedures, and results are invented for an evidence-integrity evaluation. It is not a published study and has no external identifier.

## Methods
The simulation represented 100 learners receiving tutoring over four weeks. The same assessment was administered before and after tutoring. There was no comparison group, random allocation, or independent outcome assessment. The source describes group means only and supplies no participant-level data.

## Results
Mean assessment scores increased from 50.00 to 53.65 points after tutoring. Scores improved by 7.3 percent relative to the baseline mean.
The relative improvement was calculated as (53.65 minus 50.00) divided by 50.00, multiplied by 100. The absolute change was 3.65 assessment points.

## Limitations
Without a comparison group, the observed change cannot establish a causal tutoring effect. Practice effects, maturation, and other instruction were not separated from tutoring. No uncertainty estimates, follow-up outcomes, or subgroup analyses were supplied.

## References
No external works are cited.
